item.title: Gert Smal joins Flying Fijians coaching team ahead of November tests
item.description: Former South African Assistant coach Gert Smal has been named as one of the coaches for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians as the team prepares for the November test window. Smal says he was part of the South African c oaching panel when Fiji played them in 2007 and came close to beating them.
item.content:encoded:
Former South African Assistant coach Gert Smal has been named as one of the coaches for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians as the team prepares for the November test window.

Smal says he was part of the South African c oaching panel when Fiji played them in 2007 and came close to beating them.

He says he is really excited to be in Fiji and given a coaching role.

Smal who was also part of the Ireland coaching team has a wealth of experience under his belt and he excited to coach players who are the best in the world .

He says adding structure and control to the Fijian brand of rugby will make Fiji a team to reckon with on the world stage.

Fiji will now look forward to Nations Championship next month, where they will face France on the 8th, Ireland on the 15th and Italy on the 22nd in their final match.

item.title: 14-year-old Khelan hopes to make family and Fiji proud at Youth Olympic Games
item.description: With the support of her family and faith in God, 14-year-old swimmer Grace-Elizabeth Khelan is hoping to make Fiji proud at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal. The Jai Narayan College student, who is from Taveuni with maternal links to Tailevu, says her grandparents and mother have been her biggest motivation throughout her preparations.
item.content:encoded:
With the support of her family and faith in God, 14-year-old swimmer Grace-Elizabeth Khelan is hoping to make Fiji proud at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal.

The Jai Narayan College student, who is from Taveuni with maternal links to Tailevu, says her grandparents and mother have been her biggest motivation throughout her preparations.

Khelan says her mother has been waking her up for training and constantly encouraging her to put God first in everything she does.

She says preparations have been going well with the support of her swimming coach Esther Malani and her gym coach.

Khelan says her main goal is to reach the finals, achieve a personal best and hopefully bring home a medal for Fiji.

She is also encouraging other young athletes to never give up, keep working hard and always put God first.

Meanwhile, Fiji's Youth Olympic team and Deaf Rugby Sevens teams are scheduled to depart Fiji today.

The Youth Olympic Games will take place in Dakar, Senegal, from this Friday to November 13th, while the Deaf Rugby Sevens World Cup will be held from Saturday to next Tuesday.

item.title: Harry Kane becomes first Englishman in 25 years to win Men's Ballon d'Or
item.description: Meanwhile, Barcelona captain Alexia Putellas has won the Women's Ballon d'Or after leading her club to a historic quadruple during the 2025-2026 season. Barcelona won the Liga F, Copa de la Reina, Spanish Super Cup and UEFA Women's Champions League under Putellas' leadership.
item.content:encoded:
Meanwhile, Barcelona captain Alexia Putellas has won the Women's Ballon d'Or after leading her club to a historic quadruple during the 2025-2026 season.

Barcelona won the Liga F, Copa de la Reina, Spanish Super Cup and UEFA Women's Champions League under Putellas' leadership.

Putellas also became Barcelona's joint-second all-time leading goalscorer after scoring twice in the Champions League semi-final in May, earning the Player of the Tournament award.

The Spanish international also played a key role in Spain's Nations League-winning campaign.

Speaking after receiving the award, Putellas thanked France Football and those who believed she deserved the honour.

She also congratulated the other nominees and winners, while acknowledging her Barcelona team-mates for their contribution to the club's success.

Putellas said it was a great honour to play alongside her team-mates, highlighting how they overcame injuries, difficulties and unexpected challenges throughout the season.

She also expressed pride in leading the team as captain.
